summary.text: In Apollodorus' alternate reckoning, wife of Pelias at Iolcus — daughter of Amphion — by whom the same royal brood of Acastus and the Peliades is sometimes genealogically ordered instead of through Anaxibia daughter of Bias.

Homonym guard: Apollodorus names only Amphion without further qualification; the Orchomenian king father of Chloris (`amphion-orchomenus`) stands nearest the Thessalian stemma in the same book, but the Theban lyre-king (`amphion`) remains a rival reading in the scholia.

story.text: But Pelias dwelt in Thessaly and married Anaxibia, daughter of Bias — according to some his wife was Phylomache, daughter of Amphion — and he begat a son, Acastus, and daughters, Pisidice, Pelopia, Hippothoe, and Alcestis.
